title: VNG: Common Ground
description: Ongoing work for VNG on Common Ground: the bitemporal register, the expert group of the municipal data model, the Dutch ODRL profile for federated access control and history in APIs.

config.markdown:
Common Ground is the movement through which Dutch municipalities rebuild their information systems: data at the source, separate from processes and applications. For VNG, the association of Dutch municipalities, I work on the data side of it. This is ongoing work in the public domain.

## The bitemporal register

What was a design for one register at the KVK, I work out here as a principle: every piece of data has a material timeline (when did it hold in reality) and a formal one (when was it registered). A register that keeps both right from the start can always answer what held and what was known at a given moment, and can correct without rewriting history.

The elaboration will appear in the [knowledge base](/kennisbank) (in Dutch).

items.title: Municipal data model
items.markdown: Member of the expert group of the GGM (Gemeentelijk Gegevensmodel), the data model for the municipal domain.

items.title: Federated access control
items.markdown: Member of the writing group of the Dutch ODRL profile within FTV (federated access control): recording access rules in a way that organisations can read from each other.

items.title: History in APIs
items.markdown: Member of the group within the Dutch API strategy that works out how APIs deal with history. That ties in directly with the bitemporal register.

config.markdown:
## From principle to working software

Alongside this work I built [Omnium](https://omnium.imprint-engine.nl), the model workbench that derives a register with full history from one canonical model. With it I make proofs of concept for setting up Common Ground components, among others on Fundament, the Dutch government cloud in the making.

That closes the line: a practical problem in a base register, a principle that solves it, and software that shows it works.
